chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad and Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the leather hide, so he said: 'Give it in charity or make it a prayer mat to be used in the house, and do not give it to the butchers.'
And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade giving its outer skin, its hides, and its necklaces to the butchers, and commanded him to give it in charity.'

key_terms.الإِهَابِ: Leather hide (specifically the outer skin of an animal)
key_terms.قَلاَئِدَهَا: Its necklaces (or the skin around the neck)
key_terms.مُصَلًّى: Prayer mat or place of prostration

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended way to dispose of animal hides after slaughter according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical disposal of animal hides, emphasizing their value as a resource rather than waste by permitting charity or domestic use like prayer mats. It links this ruling to the Prophet’s command to avoid giving 'Jillalah' (hides and necklaces) to butchers, reflecting a Shia legal tradition that distinguishes between the utility of the hide and the potential impurity or commercial handling by specific tradesmen. The instruction underscores the principle of maximizing benefit (*istifadah*) while maintaining ritual purity standards in household practices.
